rounds.text: Praruh Technologies Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an exceptionally modest P/E of 12x [E1] alongside an attractive EV/EBITDA of 4.55x [E11]. This low valuation completely disconnects from the company's explosive fundamental momentum, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 53% [E14] accelerating to 228% in the trailing twelve months [E15]. Profitability matches this top-line expansion, with a 3-year compounded profit growth of 64% [E16] and a 205% surge over the trailing twelve months [E17]. Furthermore, the business generates elite returns, boasting an ROE of 28.3% to 29.19% [E9, E13], a 5-year median ROE of 42% [E19], and an ROCE reaching up to 39.26% [E10], dramatically outperforming sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10]. The balance sheet remains robust and nearly debt-free with a minimal debt-to-equity ratio of 0.04x [E29, E42], while completed capital expenditure (CWIP at zero) signals that new capacity is ready to come online [E31]. Valuation models indicate the current share price only prices in a negligible 0.7% earnings growth [E37], creating a massive margin of safety against actual performance [E36, E51]. Conceded: operating cash flow dropped to Rs 0 Cr with zero cash conversion for Mar 2026 [E26, E27], and debtor days remain high at 273 days [E44].

Conceded: [E19]. Despite headline growth, severe structural cracks are visible in Praruh Technologies Ltd's cash generation and working capital health. Operating cash flow for March 2026 sits at Rs 0 Cr against reported profit, yielding a disastrous cash conversion ratio of 0.00x that strongly points toward heavily inflated receivables or accruals [E26, E27]. This cash disconnect is further compounded by ballooning debtor days reaching an alarming 273 days, while working capital requirements have nearly doubled from 47.3 days to 84.8 days [E44, E45]. Consequently, free cash flow has slipped into negative territory at Rs -1 Cr for March 2026, forcing the company to increase its borrowings from Rs 0 Cr to Rs 2 Cr by September 2026 [E28, E30]. Margin stability also remains a persistent vulnerability, with the operating margin contracting by 3 percentage points over three years to 14% alongside an inconsistent yearly trend [E22, E24]. Finally, smart money is actively retreating as domestic institutional investors have cut their stake from 6.48% to 4.21% over the past year [E33].

The bear’s focus on cash flow ignores the company’s massive operational efficiency and growth trajectory, which far outpace sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10]. While the cash conversion ratio for March 2026 was 0.00x [E26], this must be weighed against the fact that the company has successfully completed its capital expenditure cycle, with CWIP dropping to zero, signaling that new capacity is now coming online [E31]. Conceded: [E26, E27, E28]. The increase in borrowings to Rs 2 Cr is negligible given the company remains conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of only 0.04x [E29, E42]. Regarding margin concerns, the bear overlooks the most recent quarterly data showing a positive 1 percentage point expansion in operating margins compared to the year-ago quarter [E23]. Furthermore, the bear’s alarm over working capital ignores the reality that the company is currently in a high-growth phase, with sales and profit growth of 228% and 205% respectively in the trailing twelve months [E15, E17]. Finally, the retreat of domestic institutions [E33] is offset by the fact that promoters have maintained and slightly increased their significant 73.27% stake, demonstrating strong internal confidence in the business [E32].

Conceded: [E8, E9, E10]. High operational metrics cannot mask a complete failure to generate cash, evidenced by operating cash flow of Rs 0 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -1 Cr for March 2026 [E27, E28]. Claiming that zero capital work in progress resolves cash generation ignores the reality that profits are entirely detached from actual liquidity, resulting in a cash conversion ratio of 0.00x [E26]. Dismissing working capital pressures is dangerous when high debtors stretch to an alarming 273 days and overall working capital requirements nearly double from 47.3 days to 84.8 days [E44, E45]. The minor one-quarter uptick in operating margins [E23] does not offset the broader multi-year erosion where TTM operating margins have dropped by three percentage points from three years prior [E22], all while margin trends remain inconsistent [E24, E25]. Finally, while promoters hold a steady 73.27% stake [E32], domestic institutional investors have noticeably cut their holdings by 2.27 percentage points down to 4.21% [E33].
